readme: Shared HMAC test vectors for Tmesis webhook signatures (final plan 6.4,
docs/WEBHOOKS.md section 10). The sibling of keys.json, which covers the
publish-key half of the same agreement.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Two implementations must agree byte for byte: Tmesis
SIGNS every webhook and tsp-web VERIFIES it. A disagreement about the
separator, the encoding, or the hex case rejects every webhook on the
platform, and it does so at 8pm on a show night rather than in CI. Both sides
assert against THIS file.
THE RULE THAT MAKES IT WORK. The fixture is generated from the Go
implementation (go test ./internal/webhook -update) and a client NEVER edits
it. A client that cannot reproduce a row has a bug, and that is the finding,
not a reason to adjust the expected value. A shared fixture either side may
rewrite is not a contract, it is a diary.
HOW TO USE IT. For every entry in cases[]: decode secret_hex and body_hex to
bytes, build the signed string as timestamp + "." + body (one 0x2E, nothing
else), compute HMAC-SHA256 over it, hex encode lowercase, prefix with
"sha256=", and assert the result equals signature. Assert your signed string
is signed_string_length bytes first: a length mismatch finds your bug before
any MAC is computed.
THE NEGATIVE ROWS ARE THE USEFUL PART. Every entry in negative[] is a value a
CORRECT implementation must NOT produce, paired with the mistake that
produces it. If your code emits one of these, the mistake field names your
bug. They are computed over the section 4.1 example's inputs.
ENCODING NOTES. secret_hex and body_hex are authoritative and are the only
forms that can carry bytes which are not valid UTF-8; secret_utf8 and body
appear for readability. timestamp is used as its ASCII characters: do not
parse it to an integer and re-format it.

format.body: the exact bytes on the wire, never a re-serialisation. A receiver that parses the JSON and re-encodes it before verifying will fail
format.comparison: constant time, over the FULL header value including the sha256= prefix, never a prefix of it
format.mac: HMAC-SHA256(key = secret, message = signed_string), 32 raw bytes
format.secret: used as its raw bytes exactly as configured: not base64-decoded, not hex-decoded, and NOT trimmed
format.signature: the literal "sha256=" followed by mac as 64 LOWERCASE hex characters. No uppercase, no separators, no base64
format.signed_string: timestamp bytes, then one 0x2E, then body bytes. Nothing else joins them: no newline, no colon, no length prefix, no space
format.timestamp: the X-Tmesis-Timestamp header value: decimal Unix seconds, no fractional part, no leading zeros, no sign. PER ATTEMPT, not per event

cases.name: an empty body, which is still a signable request
a body that begins with the separator byte
a secret with a trailing newline, which is a DIFFERENT secret
a long timestamp, to prove the length is not assumed

negative.name: the timestamp left out of the signed string
negative.mistake: You signed the body alone. The signed string is timestamp + "." + body.

negative.name: the separator forgotten
negative.mistake: You concatenated the timestamp and the body with nothing between them. The separator is exactly one ASCII full stop, 0x2E.

negative.name: a secret with a trailing newline
negative.mistake: Your secret has a trailing newline, almost certainly from a .env file or an echo into a file. It is a different secret than you think you have.

negative.name: hashed instead of HMAC'd
negative.mistake: You hashed the body instead of computing an HMAC over the signed string.

negative.name: uppercase hex
negative.mistake: Your hex encoder emits uppercase. The header value is 64 LOWERCASE hex characters.

negative.name: the sha256= prefix omitted
negative.mistake: You sent the bare hex. The prefix names the algorithm so a future one can be added without breaking parsing, and a receiver must reject a prefix it does not recognise rather than guessing.
